title: U.S. Study to Protect Brain Health Through Lifestyle Intervention to Reduce Risk
one_line: The U.S. POINTER trial is a 2-year randomized clinical trial evaluating whether structured lifestyle interventions can protect cognitive function in older adults at increased risk of cognitive decline.
summary: This document is a ClinicalTrials.gov registry record for the U.S. POINTER trial (NCT03688126). Modeled after the Finnish FINGER study, this 2-year, randomized, triple-masked trial evaluates the cognitive benefits of lifestyle modifications in 2,000 older adults (aged 60-79) in the United States. Eligible participants are sedentary, have suboptimal MIND diet adherence, and are at elevated risk for cognitive decline, but do not currently possess cognitive impairment. Participants are randomized to either a self-guided or a structured lifestyle intervention encompassing diet, physical and cognitive exercise, and social stimulation. The primary outcome is the slope of a global cognitive function composite score (PmNTB) over two years. While the trial reached its primary completion date in May 2025, no results are posted in this registry record.

methods.population: Healthy, sedentary adults aged 60-79 with a low MIND diet score and elevated risk for cognitive decline

funding_and_conflicts: Lead sponsor: Wake Forest University Health Sciences. Collaborator: Alzheimer's Association. No conflicts stated.
limitations: This is a study registry record (protocol summary), not a peer-reviewed publication containing data or results.
No study results are available in this document to evaluate.
red_flags: The primary completion date was May 2025, but results are marked as not posted as of this record's retrieval.
